claim: OpenAI acquired Promptfoo in March 2026, raising vendor-neutrality concerns for teams using it as an independent red-teaming tool.
stance_target: eval-tooling market consolidation and vendor independence risk
quoted_support: OpenAI announced its acquisition of Promptfoo in March 2026. The open-source project continues, but teams with vendor-neutrality requirements are re-evaluating their stacks.

claim: The standard production pattern for LLM/agent quality control runs Promptfoo as a red-team CI gate (catching prompt injection, jailbreaks, PII leakage) and DeepEval as a separate metric CI gate (catching hallucination, bias, answer-relevance regressions), because the two tools cover different failure classes.
stance_target: layered eval architecture combining adversarial red-teaming with quality metric gating
quoted_support: With this topology, Promptfoo owns 'can an attacker break this'; DeepEval owns 'does this meet our quality bar.'

claim: At 10,000 evaluations/day, Promptfoo red-team plus llm-rubric assertions cost roughly $100/day in judge-model tokens versus DeepEval's 4-metric suite at roughly $300/day, because DeepEval's metrics are all LLM-judged while many Promptfoo assertions (contains, equals) require no judge call.
stance_target: eval framework cost scales with judge-model dependency, not framework choice alone
quoted_support: Promptfoo is slightly cheaper in our usage because many of its assertions don't need a judge call (e.g., contains, equals). DeepEval's metrics are all LLM-judged.

claim: Both Promptfoo and DeepEval are only approximately 85-92% accurate versus human raters, so 5-10% of flagged cases should be sampled for human review, especially for bias and toxicity judgments.
stance_target: fully automated LLM-judge evals can replace human review entirely (zero-hallucination via automation alone)
scope_conditions: LLM-as-judge grading accuracy in production use
quoted_support: Ignoring human review - both tools are ~85-92% accurate vs human raters. Sample 5-10% of flagged cases for human review, especially for bias and toxicity.

claim: Promptfoo ships 40+ red-team plugins covering direct and indirect prompt injection, jailbreaks, PII exposure, BOLA, SQL injection via LLM, excessive agency, and system-prompt leakage, with automatic adversarial test-case generation via a secondary LLM against the specific application context.
stance_target: automated red-teaming coverage breadth as a key quality-control capability for agentic systems
quoted_support: Promptfoo's red-team plugins also generate test cases automatically using a secondary LLM. You don't hand-write adversarial prompts - the tool generates them against your specific application context.
